review_candidates.title: Staff Motion Designer - 3D
review_candidates.description: In 1958, graphic designer Saul Bass opened Alfred Hitchcock's Vertigo with a spiral of color and line that told you everything about obsession before a single line of dialogue was spoken. Bass didn't think of the title sequence as a formality before the "real" movie started — he treated it as its own act of storytelling, one built entirely from motion, typography, and rhythm. He went on to define the opening moments of Psycho , North by Northwest , and Anatomy of a Murder , proving that how something moves can carry as much meaning as what it shows. Mercury believes that level of care and craft in design has been lost in modern finance and we're building a brand that brings it back. We're a financial technology company building products that feel extraordinary to use. We help people and businesses accomplish more with their money by turning banking* from a frustration into a catalyst for their ambitions. We're looking for a Staff Motion Designer to own motion at Mercury, from the launch films and product videos that introduce our biggest bets, to the systems and standards that define how motion looks and feels across every surface. This is the most senior craft role on the team: someone who sets the bar through their own work. You'll move fluidly between 3D worlds, materials, and textures for our highest-profile brand moments, and the day-to-day motion, UI, and interaction work that makes Mercury feel considered everywhere it shows up. You'll also help define how AI fits into a motion practice at Mercury — using it to move faster on pre-vis, iteration, and asset generation, while knowing exactly where craft still has to be done by hand. *Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC. In this role, you'll: Lead motion concepts for major product launches, campaigns, and brand moments, with strong 3D capability across product visualization, environments, objects, and brand worlds. Build 3D worlds, materials, and textures that give Mercury's biggest launches and brand moments a distinct, recognizable feel. Lead product storytelling, title design, typography, transitions, diagrams, and UI motion, turning complex products into simple, compelling visual stories. Define and build out Mercury's motion design system: principles for typography, pacing, transitions, product UI, sound, and interaction, plus reusable behaviors and templates that don't feel templated. Explore motion in interactive contexts, and bring an informed point of view on where AI tooling can extend the team's speed and craft without flattening it. Build and champion AI-assisted workflows for motion and 3D, from generative pre-vis and storyboarding to texture, world, and asset generation, and share what's working with the rest of Brand Studio. Evaluate new AI creative tools as they emerge and make the call on which are worth adopting into the team's pipeline versus which compromise craft. Partner with Design, Writing, Narrative, and Production from concept through delivery, and act as a key cross-functional player on the brand's biggest moments. Personally lead high-level 3D and motion craft while art-directing specialist animators, 3D artists, and studios when additional depth or scale is needed. Raise the motion craft of the broader Brand Studio through partnership, critique, and example: set the standard by doing the work, not just defining it. Protect craft and coherence across every moving expression of the brand, from a 30-second launch film to a UI micro-interaction. What you'll bring: 10+ years of professional experience in motion design, with a portfolio that shows mastery across 3D and 2D: not just execution, but conceptual thinking about how motion should move, feel, and unfold over time. Advanced proficiency in Cinema 4D, Houdini, Blender, or similar 3D tools, including materials, texturing, lighting, and world-building. Advanced proficiency in After Effects or similar 2D motion tools, with deep command of timing, easing, composition, and finishing detail. Experience building and documenting motion systems or brand guidelines, not just one-off deliverables. Comfort moving between big, high-craft brand moments and faster-moving product/UI and social work without losing quality. A track record of art-directing or mentoring other designers, animators, or outside studios. This is a craft-first role, but you lead by example and raise the bar for everyone around you. Genuine fluency with AI tooling as part of a creative practice, and a clear sense of where it helps and where craft still wins. Exposure to scripting or procedural workflows (expressions, Houdini VEX, Python) is a strong plus. Strong communication skills, able to clearly articulate concepts and creative decisions to internal teams, leadership, and external partners. A natural leader: someone who thrives in a highly collaborative environment where the best ideas drive progress, not the most powerful voices in the room. Mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities or special needs. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role. Total Rewards The total rewards package at Mercury includes base salary, equity (stock options/RSUs), and benefits. Our salary and equity ranges are highly competitive within the SaaS and fintech industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry. New hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise, geographic location, and internal pay equity relative to peers. Our target new hire base salary ranges for this role are the following : US employees in New York City, Los Angeles, Seattle, or the San Francisco Bay Area: $189,400—$236,700 USD US employees outside of New York City, Los Angeles, Seattle, or the San Francisco Bay Area: $170,400—$213,000 USD Canadian employees (any location): $179,000—$223,700 CAD

review_candidates.description: Na ABB , ajudamos os setores a operar de forma mais enxuta e sustentável — e cada pessoa aqui contribui para isso. This is a fully accountable owner's seat on a clean-core, fast-moving environment with one mandate: run this unit as fast and as AI-automated as possible. You will own the operational outcome together with one equal peer who leads finance; there is no hand-off to a support team, and no hierarchy between you. The work model for the role is: Hybrid This role is contributing to the Installation Products Division of the Electrification business area in Europe. Main stakeholders are operations and supply chain, the Finance co-owner, and the central platform team You Will Be Mainly Accountable For Co-owning the unit as one value stream and owning the non-finance operations end-to-end — run as connected flows (source-to-pay, plan-to-produce, order-to-deliver), not module silos — with full accountability for a single shared outcome alongside the Finance co-owner. Driving AI adoption at scale and stretching automation to its limit — beginning with test and regression automation against the continuous Public Cloud release cadence, then automating the operational flows themselves, deploying AI only where it moves a real metric. Running the unit fast and lean — assessing every S/4 Public Cloud release for fit and new functionality, adopting what adds value while keeping the core clean, and drawing on the central team's Developer, Integration, and Reporting services to deliver (directing and consuming them, not duplicating them). Co-owning the cross-functional seams with the Finance owner — order-to-cash and procure-to-pay run across both of you — so the end-to-end flow holds and nothing falls between operations and finance. Our team dynamics You will join a small, senior, high-ownership team — two equal co-owners running one unit — where you will be able to thrive. Qualifications For The Role A BS degree in engineering or a related technical field is a preferred. You have hands-on SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud experience — not Private, not ECC alone. You know the clean-core model, the release cadence, and what the Public Cloud will and will not allow. (This is a hard requirement.) You are driven to adopt AI at scale and push automation — test automation first — to its absolute limit; you treat a clean, fast-moving unit as a place to find the ceiling of what can run with no manual effort, not to hold a steady state. You are highly skilled across the non-finance value chain — MM, PP, IM, LE/WM, SD, QM — and you think in end-to-end flows (source-to-pay, plan-to-produce, order-to-deliver), not isolated module configuration. You have a demonstrated track record of extreme ownership — owning an outcome end to end (build and run) — and you can share a single outcome with an equal peer without building turf. You are passionate about learning and intellectually honest — comfortable with ambiguity, quick to say "I don't know" or "I was wrong," and curious enough to outpace your own defensiveness. You are at ease communicating in English; an additional European language is a plus. A degree in engineering or a related technical field is a plus. You hold a valid work authorization for the European market What's in it for you? This is a rare mandate: a fully accountable owner's seat on a modern Public Cloud unit with a single, sharp goal — run it as fast and as AI-automated as possible. You'll have the autonomy to drive AI adoption at scale and take automation as far as it will go, on a clean core built to be pushed. If your drive is to find the ceiling of what AI and automation can run — not to hold a steady state — this is the seat. Analyse CRM and clienteling activity to understand customer response and identify opportunities for optimisation. Strong data storytelling skills, with the ability to communicate complex analysis through concise presentations, visualisations and executive-ready summaries. High attention to detail with a strong commitment to data accuracy, consistency and quality. Able to work independently, manage multiple priorities and take ownership of analytical deliverables from initial question through to recommendation. review_candidates.title: Manager, Supply Chain PMO & Innovation ID217132
review_candidates.description: 该职位来源于猎聘 Role & Responsibilities Position Definition (Key Purpose of the Position) : The role strengthens the operating rhythm and transformation agenda of APAC Supply Chain Operations through three connected responsibilities: project portfolio management and project delivery, S&OP coordination, and supply chain innovation. The position works across brands, markets, functions and global teams to provide visibility, drive disciplined execution, enable leadership decisions and turn new ideas into practical business solutions. PMO and Project Delivery Manage the full APAC Supply Chain Operations project portfolio, including project intake, prioritization, governance, resource visibility, milestone tracking and portfolio reporting. Build and maintain a clear portfolio view covering project objectives, ownership, timing, dependencies, risks, investment and expected business value. Facilitate regular portfolio reviews with leadership; highlight priorities, capacity constraints, cross-project dependencies and decisions required. Act as project manager for priority APAC Supply Chain Operations projects, mainly global initiatives and market conversion projects; support other projects based on business need. Establish project charters, governance, workplans, roles, communication routines and success measures in partnership with sponsors and workstream leads. Drive delivery against agreed scope, timing and budget; manage risks, issues, changes and escalations, and ensure decisions and actions are documented and closed. Coordinate cross-functional teams including brands, planning, operations, customs and trade, technology, finance and external partners as relevant to each project. Ensure project handover, documentation, training, lessons learned and benefits tracking are completed before closure. S&OP Coordination Coordinate the APAC Supply Chain Operations S&OP meeting cycle with brand leaders, including VPs, and planning teams. Align meeting cadence, participants, agenda, inputs and pre-read materials; send invitations and communicate expectations in advance. Host and facilitate meetings to keep discussion focused on priorities, risks, decisions and actions. Capture decisions, owners and due dates during meetings; distribute clear follow-up and track actions to closure. Connect brand and supply chain stakeholders to resolve open topics, escalate decision needs and maintain continuity between meeting cycles. Continuously improve meeting effectiveness, content quality and follow-through based on stakeholder feedback and business needs. APAC Supply Chain Innovation Lead the APAC Supply Chain Operations innovation agenda, with focus on automation, AI applications, digital enablement and new ways of working. Build and maintain an innovation pipeline by collecting pain points and opportunities from markets, brands and functions. Assess opportunities based on consumer and business value, feasibility, risk, scalability, resource need and alignment with regional and global priorities. Convert selected ideas into structured pilots or projects with clear problem statements, owners, deliverables, measures and adoption plans. Partner with technology, data, process owners, users and external providers to test, deploy and scale solutions. Promote responsible and practical use of AI and automation, with appropriate human oversight, data handling and change management. Track adoption/realized benefits and lessons learned; share reusable solutions and best practices across APAC. Key Result Areas A transparent and prioritized APAC Supply Chain Operations project portfolio with timely leadership decisions. Priority projects delivered with strong governance, clear ownership and effective cross-functional coordination. S&OP meetings that are well prepared, decision focused and consistently followed through. A visible innovation pipeline that converts practical ideas into adopted solutions and measurable value. Stronger partnership across brands, markets, global teams and APAC Supply Chain Operations. Competency Requirements Strong portfolio and project management capability, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and work through a matrix organization. Effective meeting facilitation and executive stakeholder management, including confidence working with VP-level leaders. Significant exposure to project planning, project budget and financial management processes Clear written and verbal communication; able to turn complex topics into concise decisions, actions and updates. Strategic thinking combined with disciplined attention to detail and follow-through. Strong influencing, collaboration, negotiation and problem-solving skills. Comfort with ambiguity, change and experimentation; able to move from idea to practical implementation. Good understanding of supply chain operations and end-to-end business processes. Curiosity and working knowledge of automation, AI, data and digital tools; able to connect technology possibilities with business needs. Self-motivated, organized and accountable, with a strong sense of urgency and ownership. Experience 8+ years of business experience, preferably in supply chain, business operations, transformation or program management in an APAC retail or consumer-products environment. 5+ years of experience leading projects or programs involving cross-functional and senior stakeholders. Demonstrated experience in portfolio governance, complex project delivery, or business transformation. Experience coordinating S&OP or similar cross-functional business review meetings is preferred. Experience with automation, AI, process improvement or digital transformation initiatives is preferred. Academic Qualifications Bachelor's degree or equivalent. Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent project management qualification is a plus. Lean, Six Sigma, change management, agile or related qualification is a plus.
